next_state_election.name: 2026 General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections

glance_notes.text: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Alabama's voter-registration deadline is October 19. Mail absentee-ballot applications must be received by October 27, hand-delivered applications by October 29, hand-delivered absentee ballots by November 2, and mailed absentee ballots by noon on Election Day, subject to separate UOCAVA rules.
glance_notes.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — 2026 Alabama Voter Guide

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: To register to vote in Alabama, you must be a U.S. citizen, reside in Alabama, be at least 18 years old by Election Day, not have a disqualifying felony conviction unless your voting rights have been restored, and not have been legally declared mentally incompetent by a court. Alabama allows eligible residents to register or update their registration electronically through the Secretary of State, or to use a paper voter-registration form submitted to the county Board of Registrars. If you will turn 18 after the registration deadline but on or before Election Day, Alabama says you may register before the deadline and vote in that election if you meet the other qualifications.
register.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Register to Vote / Update Your Information
register.internal_note: Additional verification source: Alabama Secretary of State FAQ — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/faqs — supports the rule for a registrant who turns 18 after the registration deadline but by Election Day. Eligibility qualifications are also stated at https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/voter-registration/general-info.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Alabama's official VoterView service to confirm your voter-registration status. The service can also show your registered address, polling location, and absentee-ballot status. Alabama also says you may contact your county Board of Registrars if you are unsure whether your registration application has been processed.
check_registration.internal_note: Supplemental source: Alabama Secretary of State FAQ — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/faqs — supports contacting the county Board of Registrars when registration status is uncertain.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Alabama closes voter registration for the 14 days before an election and on Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the Secretary of State's 2026 Voter Guide lists October 19, 2026 as the voter-registration deadline. Alabama's FAQ says an otherwise eligible person who turns 18 after the registration deadline but on or before Election Day may register before the deadline and participate in that election.
deadlines.glance_value: October 19, 2026 for the November 3 General Election
deadlines.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — 2026 Alabama Voter Guide
deadlines.internal_note: Supplemental sources: Alabama Secretary of State voter-registration general information — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/voter-registration/general-info — states registration is closed for the 14 days before an election. Alabama SOS FAQ — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/faqs — supports the age-18 timing rule.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Alabama's official VoterView service to find your polling location. You can search using your registration information or use the polling-place search with your residential address. The Secretary of State's 2026 Voter Guide also directs voters to the My Voting Information service to verify their polling place. For municipal-election polling-place information, the guide directs voters to the city clerk.
polling_place.internal_note: Supplemental source: 2026 Alabama Voter Guide — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/election-2026/2026-VoterGuide.pdf — supports the municipal-election city-clerk distinction.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: At an Alabama polling place, provide your name to a poll worker and present an acceptable form of photo identification. If you do not have valid photo ID, you may cast a provisional ballot, or you may vote a regular ballot if two election officials positively identify you as an eligible voter on the poll list and sign the required sworn affidavit. Polls are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.; polling places in the Eastern Time Zone operate on Eastern Time unless the statutory exception for certain polling places in Chambers or Lee County is used. A person who attempts to join the voting line after 7:00 p.m. may not vote.
election_day.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — 2026 Alabama Voter Guide
election_day.internal_note: Supplemental sources: Alabama SOS Photo Voter ID — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/voter/voter-id — supports provisional-ballot and two-election-official identification alternatives. Code of Alabama §17-9-6 — https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/code-of-alabama?section=17-9-6 — supports the Eastern Time Zone rule and Chambers/Lee County exception.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Alabama polling places open at 7:00 a.m. and close at 7:00 p.m. Polling places in areas operating on Eastern Time use Eastern Time. State law allows the county commissions in Chambers County and Lee County to exclude a polling place from that Eastern-Time requirement by resolution, in which case that polling place operates according to Central Time.
polling_hours.glance_value: 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.; local time rule varies in limited Chambers/Lee County cases
polling_hours.source_name: Code of Alabama §17-9-6 — Time of Holding Elections

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Alabama's current Secretary of State voter materials describe absentee voting for voters who meet specified eligibility reasons and provide procedures for applying for and casting an absentee ballot before Election Day. This section is being held in review rather than making a categorical statement about whether Alabama offers a separate general early-voting program, because the official sources reviewed for this record did not provide a direct current statement establishing that negative.
early_voting.glance_value: See absentee-voting rules; early-voting classification under review
early_voting.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Absentee Voting Information
early_voting.flagged_reason: No direct current official source was located that affirmatively states whether Alabama has a separate general early-voting program; no absence-based conclusion is being published as fact.
early_voting.internal_note: The 2026 SOS absentee materials provide pre-Election-Day absentee procedures but do not themselves establish a categorical 'no early voting' statement. Introduced early-voting bills were not treated as proof of current law. Independent checker should specifically seek a current affirmative SOS or controlling statutory source before this section is marked verified.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Alabama absentee voting is available to voters who meet one of the state's listed eligibility reasons, including expecting to be absent from the county on Election Day, qualifying illness or disability, certain voters living outside their county such as college students, election officers or poll watchers assigned elsewhere, voters working a required shift of 10 hours or more that coincides with polling hours, qualifying caregivers, and certain incarcerated voters who have not been convicted of a felony involving moral turpitude. Applications sent by mail must be received by the county Absentee Election Manager no later than 7 days before the election; hand-delivered applications are due no later than 5 days before the election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, those dates are October 27 and October 29. A mailed absentee ballot must be received by noon on Election Day; a hand-delivered ballot must be received by close of business, but no later than 5:00 p.m., on the day before the election. Alabama also provides emergency and UOCAVA procedures with different rules in qualifying circumstances.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Excuse required; Nov. 3 election application deadlines: Oct. 27 by mail / Oct. 29 by hand
absentee_mail.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Absentee Voting Information
absentee_mail.internal_note: Supplemental source: 2026 Alabama Voter Guide — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/election-2026/2026-VoterGuide.pdf — supplies the exact 2026 General Election calendar dates. UOCAVA exceptions are intentionally summarized here and detailed in military_overseas.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Alabama generally requires voters to present an approved photo ID when voting in person, and voters requesting an absentee ballot generally submit a copy of approved photo ID with the application unless an exception applies. Approved forms include qualifying driver's or nondriver IDs, Alabama Photo Voter ID, other state-issued photo ID, federal photo ID, U.S. passport, qualifying government employee ID, qualifying college or university student or employee ID, military ID, and tribal ID. A voter without acceptable photo ID at the polls may cast a provisional ballot; alternatively, a voter on the poll list may vote a regular ballot if two election officials positively identify the voter and sign a sworn affidavit. A voter whose ballot is provisional because of missing identification has until 5:00 p.m. on the Friday after the election to provide valid identification to the county Board of Registrars. Alabama provides free photo voter ID options for eligible voters who lack an accepted form.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID generally required; provisional and two-official identification alternatives exist
voter_id.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Photo Voter ID
voter_id.internal_note: Supplemental sources: 2026 Photo Voter ID Guide — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/election-2026/PhotoVoterIDGuide.pdf — supports the Friday-after-election 5 p.m. provisional-ID deadline and free-ID options. Code of Alabama §17-9-30 — https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/code-of-alabama?section=17-9-30 — supports absentee-ID requirements and federal-law exceptions. SOS valid-ID page — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/photo-voter-id/valid-ids — contains the current detailed accepted-ID list.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Alabama says accessible voting machines are available at every polling site on Election Day. Voters who are disabled or age 70 or older may move to the front of the polling-place line after notifying a poll worker. A voter may request assistance from a person of the voter's choice except the voter's employer, an agent of the employer, or an officer or agent of the voter's union; a poll worker may also assist. Alabama also has absentee procedures for voters with qualifying disabilities, including a permanent-disability absentee application that can cover county, state, and federal elections during the applicable period described by the Secretary of State.
accessible_voting.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Assistance for Voters with Disabilities

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Alabama provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for qualifying military members, their spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living overseas under UOCAVA. The Federal Post Card Application (FPCA) can be used in the process, and qualifying voters may request electronic delivery of ballots. Voters located outside the territorial limits of the United States who meet Alabama's requirements may also return voted ballots electronically. Alabama also recognizes the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup ballot for qualifying UOCAVA voters. UOCAVA voters are exempt from Alabama's ordinary photo-ID requirement for absentee voting under the state's voter-ID law.
military_overseas.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Military & Overseas Absentee Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: Supplemental source: Alabama Secretary of State 2026 Voter Guide — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/election-2026/2026-VoterGuide.pdf — states the UOCAVA photo-ID exemption. Code of Alabama §17-9-30 also contains the federal-law ID exception.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students are subject to Alabama's ordinary voter-registration qualifications, including Alabama residence. Alabama's absentee rules specifically recognize a registered Alabama voter living outside the county — including a college student — as an absentee-voting eligibility category. The state's absentee application also identifies a student at an educational institution outside the county of the student's permanent residence who cannot vote at the usual polling place on Election Day as an absentee category. Students should use their actual voting residence when registering and update their registration when their voting residence changes.
student_voting.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Absentee Voting Information
student_voting.internal_note: Supplemental sources: voter-registration qualifications — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/voter-registration/general-info. Alabama generic absentee application — https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/absentee-forms/Generic_Absentee_Application_Fillable.pdf — expressly includes students outside their county of permanent residence. This section intentionally avoids broader claims about student domicile that were not directly established by the official election sources reviewed.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Alabama publishes official sample ballots through the Secretary of State for elections as they become available. The Secretary of State's 2026 Election Information page currently provides sample-ballot links for earlier 2026 elections and is the official location for 2026 election materials. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the page currently lists certified candidate and constitutional-amendment materials; voters should check the official 2026 Election Information page for General Election sample ballots when posted.
sample_ballot.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — 2026 Election Information
sample_ballot.flagged_reason: The official 2026 election page was verified, but a November 3 General Election sample-ballot link was not surfaced in the current page content reviewed on August 30, 2026.
sample_ballot.internal_note: Recheck as the November 3 General Election approaches. The page already contains General Election candidate certifications and statewide constitutional-amendment certification, but this record does not claim the General Election sample ballots are currently posted.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Alabama Secretary of State, Elections Division. Physical address: 600 Dexter Ave., State Capitol Building, Suite E-208, Montgomery, AL 36130. Elections Division phone: 334-242-7210; toll-free: 1-800-274-8683; fax: 334-242-2444. The Secretary of State's Alabama Votes contact page also lists a mailing address of P.O. Box 5616, Montgomery, AL 36103-5616.
contact.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The general SOS Contact Us page currently lists the Elections Division at State Capitol Building, Suite E-208. A separate Alabama Votes contact page, https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/contact-us, lists physical address 600 Dexter Ave., Suite E-206 and the same phone/fax numbers. Because the official pages conflict on suite number, the reader-facing content uses E-208 from the current general Contact Us page but this discrepancy should be independently checked. If strict conflict handling is preferred, change this section to in_review before import.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Alabama Votes, operated by the Alabama Secretary of State, is the state's central election-information hub. It links to voter registration and registration updates, My Voting Information/VoterView, absentee voting, election information, upcoming elections, photo voter ID, district maps, and statewide constitutional-amendment information. VoterView provides registration status, polling-location and absentee-ballot-status tools. For county-specific election administration, the Secretary of State also provides directories for Boards of Registrars, Judges of Probate, Circuit Clerks, and Absentee Election Managers.
official_resources.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State — Alabama Votes
official_resources.internal_note: Supplemental action tool: Alabama VoterView — https://myinfo.alabamavotes.gov/VoterView. County/local contacts are linked throughout the Alabama Votes voter pages.
